1.title: Protecting Data
1.text: Welcome to Module ten: Protecting Data. It covers the exam area Security Architecture. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do six things. Data types and states. Data classification. Methods used to secure data. Data protection roles. Data handling and life cycle. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Security Architecture (nineteen percent). Exam format: up to ninety questions in ninety minutes; a score of seven hundred fifty on a scale of one hundred to nine hundred passes. Validated against: the official Comp T I A Security plus S Y zero eight oh one V eight exam objectives.

1.title: Data types and states
1.text: Data types and states. Data types. Items: Structured. Meaning: Organized in fields such as a database table. Items: Unstructured. Meaning: No fixed format: documents, email, images, video. Data states. Items: Data at rest. Meaning: Stored (disk, database, backup): protect with encryption and access control. Items: Data in use. Meaning: Being processed in memory: protect with access control and secure processing. Items: Data in transit. Meaning: Moving over a network: protect with T L S, V P N (virtual private network), I P sec.

1.title: Data types and states, continued
1.text: Data types and states. The figure shows this: The three data states: at rest, in use and in transit, with a protection for each. Exam tip: At rest equals stored (encrypt the disk or database). In transit equals moving (T L S or V P N). In use equals in memory (hardest to protect).

1.title: Data classification
1.text: Data classification. Classification labels data by how sensitive it is, so it gets the right level of protection. Public. Safe to share with anyone. Restricted. Limited to specific groups. Confidential. Harm if disclosed outside the company. Sensitive. Needs care: for example personal or financial data. Secret or Top secret. Government-style high levels: serious or grave damage if exposed. Critical. Essential to operations: loss halts the business. Organizations choose their own scheme; the key is applying handling rules to each level.

1.title: Methods used to secure data
1.text: Methods used to secure data. Encryption. Meaning: Scrambles data with a key. Reversible?: Yes, with the key. Hashing. Meaning: One-way fingerprint. Reversible?: No. Masking. Meaning: Hides part of a value ( -one thousand two hundred thirty-four ). Reversible?: No (display only). Tokenization. Meaning: Replaces a value with a random token; the real value is in a secure vault. Reversible?: Yes, through the vault. Obfuscation. Meaning: Makes data hard to understand. Reversible?: Often weak.

1.title: Methods used to secure data, continued
1.text: Methods used to secure data. Deidentification. Meaning: Removes personal identifiers. Reversible?: Not meant to be. Filtering. Meaning: Blocks or removes sensitive content from data flows. Reversible?: n or a. Data transpose. Meaning: Rearranges data (for example swapping fields). Reversible?: Depends.

1.title: Methods used to secure data, continued
1.text: Methods used to secure data. The figure shows this: Masking, tokenization and hashing compared with the same card number. Exam tip: Tokenization swaps the value for a token stored with a vault; it is common for payment cards. Masking is display protection. Hashing cannot be reversed. Deidentification supports privacy.

1.title: Data protection roles
1.text: Data protection roles. Data owner. Accountable for the data; decides classification and access. Data custodian. Operates and protects the data day to day (technical controls, backups). Data steward. Ensures data quality and proper use under policy. Data operator. Processes data on instructions. Data controller. Decides why and how personal data is processed. Data subprocessor. A third party that processes data for a processor.

1.title: Data handling and life cycle
1.text: Data handling and life cycle. Handling. Endpoints, marking and labeling, geofencing (limit by location), data location, data placement. Life cycle. Creation, management, distribution, retention, disposal. Compliance. Standards, health data, personal information, financial, child or minor data, intellectual property, legal data. Exam tip: Disposal must be secure (shredding, cryptographic erase, degaussing). The data owner classifies; the custodian implements controls. A controller decides purposes; a processor acts on its behalf.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Fabrikam Outdoors wants to keep real card numbers out of its order system but still allow refunds. Which method fits best? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Tokenization. Tokenization replaces the card number with a token while the real value stays in a secure vault for authorized use.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A call center screen shows only the last four digits of a card. Which method is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Masking. Showing part of a value and hiding the rest is masking.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Customer files on a laptop are encrypted with full disk encryption. Which data state does this protect? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Data at rest. Stored data is data at rest, and disk encryption protects it.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Who decides how a company's customer database is classified and who may access it? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Data owner. The data owner is accountable for the data and sets its classification and access rules.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. An administrator backs up and secures the database servers according to the owner's rules. Which role is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Data custodian. The custodian operates and protects the data using technical controls.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. A company restricts who can download files depending on the country they are in. Which handling technique is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Geofencing. Geofencing limits access or use based on location.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Name the three data states. Answer: At rest, in use and in transit. Question two. What is the difference between structured and unstructured data? Answer: Structured data has fixed fields; unstructured data has no fixed format. Question three. Which method is reversible only through a vault? Answer: Tokenization.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What is the data steward responsible for? Answer: Data quality and proper use under policy. Question five. Name the five stages of the data life cycle. Answer: Creation, management, distribution, retention and disposal. Question six. What is a data controller? Answer: The party that decides why and how personal data is processed.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. States: at rest (stored), in use (memory), in transit (network). Classification: public, restricted, confidential, sensitive, secret, top secret, critical. Methods: encryption, hashing, masking, tokenization (vault), obfuscation, deidentification, filtering, transpose. Roles: owner (accountable), custodian (operates), steward (quality), operator, controller, subprocessor. Handling: labeling, geofencing, location, placement; life cycle ends with secure disposal. In the next module, we continue the course.
